publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper presents a high precision DAC with seamless switch technique for large array CMOS image sensor to calibrate column fixed pattern noise and black level. Through the deep analysis on non-ideal factor and error source of piecewise DAC in multichannel, the high precision seamless switch technique has been researched. The adaptive signal chain switch technique according to the high to low subsection is developed in this paper, so the seamless switch is realized, and the convert accuracy is boosted. A prototype high intrinsic DR and low column FPN CMOS image sensor chip consisting of 64M 4T active pixel sensor (APS) array was designed and fabricated in 55nm CMOS 1P4M standard process, 75dB intrinsic DR and 0.06% column-to-column fixed pattern noise are achieved.

articleTitle: Simulation of that the Rotated Square Holes Effect on the Shunt Capacitive RF MEMS Switch
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of holes with different rotation angles on radio frequency micro electro mechanical system (RF MEMS) switch are analyzed. In micro- scale, the holes play important role on the performance of the shunt capacitive RF MEMS switch. This paper uses the conventional RF MEMS switch struture and compares with proposed structures to see if the roated holes could improve the performance. From the computed result, it can be found that the roated holes can certainly improve the performance when the roated angle is 30°, in which the actuarion time is reduced by 0.1 μs.

articleTitle: Experimentation and Simulation for Cap Gate AlGaN/GaN HEMT Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Experimental and simulation I-V characteristics of the cap gate high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) are reported. The two-dimensional simulations results are in conformity with the realistic HEMT perfectly, indicating reliable and acceptable of the TCAD simulation method in GaN-based devices. Depending on this, further researches on the cap gate HEMT are carried out by TCAD software, which analyzes the impact of recessed depth of gate barrier, the dimension of L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</sub> and cap gate structure on GaN HEMT performances.

articleTitle: The Investigation of TiO2 Nanostructures on Performance of Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: In this work, we have studied the effects of the compact TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (c-TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) and mesoscopic TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (mp-TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) layers on the performance of the perovskite based solar cells (PSCs). It is found that the increased interfacial area between the mesoscopic electron transport layer (ETL) and perovskite can enhance the device efficiency, particularly for the fill factor. We have then synthesized TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanorods (TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-NR) and incorporated it into PSCs, in which the interfacial area between perovskite and TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-NA is further increased. A hysteresis-free PSC with the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19 % can be obtained by using TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-NR as the ETL. The results of femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) clearly show that the carrier extraction efficiency is significantly enhanced due to substantial increase of the interfacial area between the perovskite and ETL nanostructures, resulting in a reduction in carrier diffusion distance.

articleTitle: Nanoelectrode Arrays Based on Vertically Aligned Carbon Nanofibers for Dielectrophoretic Capture and Detection of Pathogens
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Dielectrophoresis (DEP) is a technique that utilizes electric field to manipulate polarizable particles. Here we summarize our studies on developing a nanostructured DEP device for capture of bacterial cells and viral particles. A high magnitude non-uniform electric field was produced in a microfluidic channel utilizing a nanoelectrode array made of vertically aligned carbon nanofibers versus a macroscopic indium tin oxide counter electrode in a “points-and-lid” configuration. Reversible DEP capture was demonstrated with E. coli bacterial cells (~1-2 micron in size) and viral particles (bacteriophage T4r and vaccinia virus, ~80-200 nm in size) with an AC voltage (100 Hz to 1 MHz). The DEP technique can Ue coupled with surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) reporter for rapid and specific detection of E. coli cells.

articleTitle: Low voltage low power full adder for baseband circuits in wireless systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A low voltage low power 1-bit full adder is proposed for digital baseband in wireless systems. The full adder adopts stacked NMOS transmission gates and inverters as the building block. Leakage power is well controlled and desirable power-delay product (PDP) is achieved. When the adder is implemented in TSMC 65 nm low-VT process, the leakage power is only 1.43 nW at 0.4 V power supply, while PDP is 4.84 nW*ns. Good noise margin is also obtained at low voltages.

articleTitle: High Speed Energy Efficient Optical Receiver
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper describes the design techniques of high speed, energy efficient optical receivers, covering from the front-end amplifier to the post clock and data recovery circuit (CDR). An integration type optical receiver incorporating with a current boost preamplifier and a baud rate CDR is proposed to improve the receiver sensitivity as well as its energy efficiency. A fully integrated experimental prototype is implemented in a TSMC 40 nm CMOS technology that achieves a high energy efficiency of 2.1 pJ/bit at 25 Gbps operation.

Author Keywords: Baud Rate Clock and Data Recovery Circuit

articleTitle: Degradation Behaviors of Driving Thin-Film Transistors in Active-Matrix Organic Light-Emitting Diode Displays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: The reliability of driving TFTs of an AMOLED display is investigated and studied. The simulated driving voltage stress is proposed and applied in poly-Si TFTs. The degradation shows a two-stage degradation behavior. Incorporated with transient simulation, the degradation mechanisms are tentatively discussed.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: Improved Performance of Pentacene OTFT by using Hybrid Oxide of Nd and Hf as Gate Dielectric
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Pentacene organic thin-film transistors (OTFTs) adopting high-k NdON, HfON and NdHfON as gate dielectrics are fabricated. Their electrical and physical characteristics are compared. With appropriate Nd/Hf ratio in the dielectric, the OTFT with NdHfON gate dielectric can achieve improved performance such as a carrier mobility of 1.1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/V·s and a small threshold voltage of -1.20 V. The AFM results of the pentacene layer and the dielectric layer reveal that both improved dielectric and pentacene morphologies lead to the higher carrier mobility of the device.

articleTitle: A Novel Cascode Mixer for NB-IoT Transceiver System in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: NB-IoT is a FDD system. Its TX & RX are operated at a fixed frequency offset at the same time. Conventional architecture builds 2 PLLs to support FDD. This paper presents a new architecture which only needs one PLL. Its receiver introduces a novel cascode-mixer structure (Cascaded by two current-mode passive mixers driven by 25% duty-cycle quadrature clocks). The cascode mixer makes two times mixing of RF signals using the LO1 produced by the PLL and the LO2 from the crystal reference. It achieves 18.7dB noise figure and +8.13 dBm IP1dB in simulation with a commercial 65nm RFCMOS process. It consumes 2.8mA from a 1.2V supply. IQ phase mismatch correction is also implemented in this design.

articleTitle: A noval fast-locking ADPLL based on Newton's Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Based on the idea of Newton's Method, a new structure of AllDigital Phased-Locked Loop(ADPLL) is proposed. The ADPLL is made up of a fully customized frequency comparator, controller and digital-controlled oscillator (DCO). The proposed structure and locking method are different from the traditional one. RTL simulation results show that the lockin time of the proposed ADPLL with 2 different output frequenciesis, is much faster than the traditional structure, only N reference clock cycle, saving at least 86%.

articleTitle: Enhancement Of Positive Bias Stress Stability For IGZO TFTs By A CAAC Gd-AZO Bulk Layer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A c-axis-aligned crystalline Gd-Al-Zn-O (CAAC Gd-AZO) layer is implemented at the interface between the active layer and dielectric to enhance positive gate bias stress (PBS) stability of In-Ga-Zn-O thin film transistors (IGZO TFTs). The Gd-AZO bulk layer diminishes the root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of the IGZO back channel layer, which leads to the smaller threshold voltage shift (ΔV<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub>) of the Gd-AZO/IGZO TFTs than the IGZO/IGZO TFTs.

articleTitle: A Novel Zero Current Detector for Single-Inductor Double-Output DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel zero current detector (ZCD) for single-inductor double-output (SIDO) DC-DC converter which works in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM). The proposed ZCD circuit can accurately acquires inductor voltage and output voltage, and deal with these voltage signals to implement a high speed and high precision controller to avoid reverse current. The test chip was simulated by 110nm CMOS process with input voltage of 0.8V to 1.5V. Simulation results demonstrate a high efficiency of 88.5% at input voltage of 1.5V.

articleTitle: A Normally-off P-Gate AlGaN/GaN HEMT for High Power Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel normally-off p-GaN gate AlGaN/GaN HEMT on AlGaN buffer with an InGaN layer inserted between GaN channel and AlGaN buffer is proposed and investigated by Sentaurus TCAD simulation tool. A higher drain current (lower R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sub>) in the on-state and higher breakdown voltage (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Br</sub>) are achieved simultaneously. The V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Br</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sub> is increased by 34.8%.

articleTitle: Ti Film Thickness Influences on the Back Channel Etched Amorphous InGaZnO4 Thin Film Transistors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Back channel etched (BCE) amorphous InGaZnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>(a–IGZO) thin film transistors are fabricated, in which Ti thin film is employed as a protective layer for a-IGZO. The optimal Ti thickness is found to be 4-5 nm, and a-IGZO will be well protected and excellent transfer curves can be obtained after O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma and annealing treatment. Besides, by the introduction of the Ti layer, the devices obtain better stress stability.

articleTitle: High-efficiency CMOS power amplifier with a folded proportional combining structure and adaptive power mode control
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A novel folded proportional series combining transformer used for linear power amplifier (PA) is proposed in this paper. The power delivery efficiency is significantly enhanced, especially at power back off region. Using a standard $0.18- \mu \mathrm {m}$ CMOS process, a fully integrated dual-channel PA was designed. With adaptive channel control, the PA can achieve a wide power adjustment range and better efficiency at power back off, which is suitable for high peak-average power ratio (PAPR) modulation applications.

articleTitle: Back-Propagation Neural Network based on Analog Memristive Synapse
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Due to the low power consumption and its feasibility of highly scalable crossbar arrays, memristors have recently arouse a great interest to mimic the principles and operations of biological brains in neuromorphic computing. Two kinds of memristors (TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-based memristor and Ta<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5-x</sub>-based memristor) are separately combined into synapses to simulate a three-layer perceptron neural network operated by back-propagation algorithms on MATLAB platform. The device to device variations are considered in terms of the model's accuracy. Moreover, the effect of the target values and the initial weights on the final weight distribution are discussed.

articleTitle: Effects of High Temperature Treatment on SiO2 Patterned Mask on Si Substrate
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: The relationship of the stability of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> patterned mask with different thickness was investigated in this paper. The optical microscopy and SEM images shown that the SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> patterned mask with 300nm thickness were not only disappeared from the Si substrate, but also over-reacted with the Si substrates, after the high-temperature treatment with a vacuum atmosphere, so that the surface of the Si substrate became roughened; While, the SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> patterned mask with a thickness of 500 nm can be maintained after being processed under the same conditions.

articleTitle: Facile Fabrication of Porous Carbon Materials Derived from Pleurotus Eryngii for Supercapacitor Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Porous carbon materials derived from pleurotus eryngii were successfully synthesized by carbonization and activation. The specific surface area of the obtained porous carbons reached up to 3255 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. The electrode exhibited a maximal specific capacitance of 236 F g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and excellent long-term cycle stability with 94% capacitance retention after 6000 cycles at the current density of 2 A g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Therefore, pleurotus eryngii is demonstrated as an attractive biomass precursor of carbon materials for supercapacitor applications.

articleTitle: An interface pressure measurement system for medical compression stockings
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper proposes an interface pressure measurement system for medical compression stockings (MCS). A prototype system is developed and proved to be effective in the MCS interface pressure measuring applications. By employing a soft and thin air pouch to sense the interface pressure generated by MCS compressing onto skin, patients don't feel uncomfortable obviously. Due to the miniature size of the device, the system is suitable to be assembled into wearable pressure monitoring systems in the future.

Author Keywords: pressure measurement, medical compression stockings, air pouch

articleTitle: T-chip, Electrochemical biosensor platform based on the electron tunneling: Role and effect of the back-filling material
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: The concept of the electrochemical biosensor platform based on the electron tunneling (T-chip) is suggested. A pair of a probe peptide and a target protease protein (biomarker) which indicates the severity of the disease (carcinoma and tissue tumor) is introduced. The cleaving event of the probe peptide is utilized to detect the existence of the biomarkers and to measure their reaction activity. The redox molecule, Methylene blue (MB), is functionalized at the end of the peptide sequence providing the electron states where the electron flows in and out. The main strategy of detecting biomarkers is measuring the change of the tunneling current between the metal electrode and the MB states. To maintain stable electrical characteristics of the sensor and to optimize detection performance, not only the probe peptide itself but also the back-filling material, Mercapto-ol-series (MCX) is important. In this paper, the key role of the back-filing material and its length effect on the detection performance is investigated.

articleTitle: Large Area Perovskite Solar Cell via Two-step Ultrasonic Spray Deposition
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: We report a controllable two-step deposition method for fabricating perovskite solar cells. The perovskite light absorption layers were prepared by the reaction of spin-coated PbI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and spray-coated CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>I. The CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>I precursor solution is spray-coated under ambient atmosphere, which gives a better control of the perovskite morphology and a completed reaction. Using this method, we achieve a PCE of 11.4% at a 0.04 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> device area, and 8.8% at a 1.16cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> device area.

articleTitle: A Low Power High Frequency Quantizer Based on the Time-to-Digital Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This article proposed a high frequency quantizer which can be used in continue-time delta-sigma modulator (CTDSM). The proposed quantizer is constituted by voltage-to-time converter (VTC) and time-to-digital converter (TDC). The voltage is converted to pulse by VTC first and then the pulse is converted to digital output by TDC. With the new structure of the TDC, the hardware and power consumption is reduced. Using UMC 65nm CMOS technology, the proposed 3bit-quantizer consumes 0.298mW with 260MHz working frequency.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Liquid Loading Effect on the Flexible Acoustic Wave Devices for in-Liquid Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Flexible electronics has many unique qualities such as bendable, lightweight and low-cost fabrication, and are particularly suitable for biosensor applications. Biosensors based on acoustic wave devices feature high resolution, digital output, and wireless operation. In this paper, we address the important issue when the flexible acoustic wave devices are used in liquid for sensing applications. A two-port resonator structure is proposed to implement the flexible acoustic wave device. Electrical measurements were conducted for the same device under various environments, and the liquid loading induced lowering of the quality factor are analyzed.

articleTitle: A Wireless Power-Efficient Charger Chip with Closed-Loop Controlling Mechanism for Implantable Biomedical System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: The requirement of fast, steady and safe chargers has become the most important issue for implantable power management. This work proposes a closed-loop control charger consisted of a high efficient rectifier, charging control circuit and PWM signal generators. It makes the charging voltage automatically follow the battery voltage by a feedback loop, which reduces the energy consumption caused by large voltage difference between the constant charging voltage and battery voltage. A prototype was fabricated in 0.8μm HV CMOS technology, and the measured maximum overall efficiency is 70.67%.

articleTitle: Modified Deep Learning Approach for Layout Hotspot Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: With the fast development of very large scale integrated circuits (VLSI) lithography, hotspot detection is playing a crucial role in semiconductor design process. Nowadays pattern matching and machine learning achieve satisfactory performance, but because of the extreme scaling of transistor feature node and continue growing of layout pattern complexity, these traditional approaches may be ineligible for the tough task. In this paper, we introduce a hotspot detection method based on carefully designed deep learning network. At the same time, carefully analyzing the functionalities of different network layer types, we argue that pooling layer isn't necessary for hotspot detection and can be replaced for better performance. On the other hand, since hotspot patterns are always in the minority in VLSI mask design, we apply folding, rotating and mirror-flipping for data augmentation of hotspot clips for seven times offline before training. The modified deep neural network can achieve comparable performance on the ICCAD 2012 contest benchmark.

articleTitle: Resistive Switching Memory towards Embedded Application in 28 nm Node and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This work addresses the development of 1Mb embedded RRAM macro on 28 nm standard logic platform. Careful evaluation on thermal stability and reading disturbance of resistance in various resistance ranges were performed in Macro.Compared with conventional eFLASH, this BEOL based RRAM technology provides a competitive solution for low power, low cost embedded application in 28 nm node and beyond.

articleTitle: Large-area Visible-blind 4H-SiC Ultraviolet Avalanche Photodiode with High Gain and Low Bias Voltage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: Based on the separate absorption and multiplication (SAM) structure, visible-blind 4H-SiC ultraviolet avalanche photodiodes (APDs) with large active area (400 μm diameter) were designed and fabricated in this work. The results show that high optical gain of 1.7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> and low bias voltage (i.e. low breakdown voltage) of 50.6 V are achieved at room temperature. Additionally, a maximum quantum efficiency of 30% is obtained at 270nm with the reverse bias voltage of 10 V, which can be further improved by optimizing device structures.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Single-Chip Internet of Things Transponder with Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A low-power single-chip Internet of things transponder that provides automotive security passive keyless entry is presented. To guarantee high reliability under poor conditions, the transponder can switch the power supply between the low-frequency field and its internal battery seamlessly when using the proposed intelligent power management scheme. Measurement results show the improved full-wave rectifier produces 72% high-efficiency conversion from low-frequency AC to DC voltage for energy harvesting, and an enhanced amplitude-shift keying demodulation guarantees reliable data transmission at low power.

articleTitle: Visible Light Communication System-on-a-Chip
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper reviews a fully integrated transceiver designed in an 180nm BCD process for light-emitting diode (LED) based visible light communication (VLC) system-on-a-chip (SoC). The VLC transceiver SoC consists of Manchester encoder/decoder, high accuracy bandgap reference, phase lock loop (PLL), multistage amplifier, trans-impedance amplifier (TIA), LED driver and ESD protection. A feed-forward equalizer is used to boost the LED bandwidth for high data rate wireless streaming. Measurement demonstrates wireless streaming of data through visible light using commercial LEDs.

articleTitle: Carrier Injection Mechanism of Metal-MoS2 Ohmic Contact in MoS2 FETs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: In order to enhance the carrier injection ofMoS2 field effect transistors (FETs,) understanding the injection mechanism of metal MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> contacts is essential. In this work, MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (FETs) with Ti and Sc electrodes were faUricated and characterized, respectively. The carrier injection mechanism was studied from the perspective of the tunneling models. With the narrower barrier width, the MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> contact shows a different injection mechanism from that of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, making Sc a promising improvement as MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> FETs electrodes.

articleTitle: Short Range LFMCW System for Automobile Reversing Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A 77GHz LFMCW (Linear Frequency Modulated Continuous Waveform) radar system for automobile reversing application is presented. To improve the radar accuracy of distance and speed, several algorithm techniques such as variable-cycle triangle wave, combined amplitude and phase algorithm are introduced. And the radar can work under the influence of interference because of the clutter map technique. The radar system has been verified by Matlab.

articleTitle: Local Modification of Defective Edge Hamiltonian for Graphene Nanoribbon Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: The impact of edge defect on C-C bond is revealed to be localized in short range by ab initio calculation. Thus we propose a local modification method to construct the tight-bind (TB) Hamiltonian. Except for the edge parameter correction, this method considers the local C-C bond distortion and the diversity of different armchair GNRs. It is demonstrated that this method significantly reduces TB fitting errors with two typical GNR edge defects. In addition, using the modified Hamiltonian, device simulation results are shown.

articleTitle: Current Enhancement of Graphene-Inserted Tunneling Contact IGZO TFT
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper presents a method to enhance the on-current (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sub>) of the graphene-inserted tunneling contact IGZO thin film transistors (TCTFTs) by introducing a thin and highly-doped region at the contact. The highly-doped region is formed by post N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> annealing to generate donor-like defects near the IGZO surface. The introduction of this region can increase the I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sub> by ~ 7 times without affecting the off current I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</sub>, leading to a much higher on/off current ratio. Steeper sub-threshold slope of the TCTFT compared with the normal TFT is also observed.

articleTitle: Design of High Performance XOR and XNOR Logic Gates without MOS Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A design of high performance and area-efficient XOR and XNOR logic gates based on memristors is proposed, which consuming only 3 memristor cells and 3 clock cycles, 4 memristor cells and 4 clock cycles, respectively. The input of the gates is applied by voltage, and the output is presented as resistance value of the output cell. The proposed gates are MOS-less, and can be integrated into the 3D crossbar memristor array.

articleTitle: A Low Power Signal Acquisition Channel with a Novel Systematic Power Minimization Scheme
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: This paper implements an analog front-end with a proposed systematic power minimization scheme to reduce both the analog front-end power consumption and the data converter consumption without any performance degradation. The scheme creatively uses intensive pulse signals from a counterbased digital control circuits in a SAR ADC to finely tune up/down the amplifier output driving ability. The amplifier's output stage is configurable and divided into several slices in parallel. Each output slice can be individually controlled by the control signal from ADC. The paper implements the systematic power minimization scheme with an 8-bit SAR ADC and a configurable amplifier. The simulation results verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Novel Cryo-controlled Nucleation Technique for High-efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid State Circuits (EDSSC)
abstract: A novel cryo-controlled nucleation technique is developed to grow mixed halide perovskite for solar cells (PSCs). The abrupt decrease in the ambient temperature results in a supersaturation condition in the precursor film prepared by the spin coating process, leading to form uniform nucleation sites for subsequent crystal growth. The low temperature ambient retards the pre-mature crystallization of the perovskite film in the early stage before a uniform seed layer is obtained. This film deposition approach ensures excellent uniformity of the nucleation layers and, subsequently, higher quality perovskite films. A power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.4 % for the champion PSC can be achieved by the proposed perovskite growth technique.
